# Wave 1 (singleton): CR, one repair, and the SR→CR reroute

Checkout: `/workspace/project`. `WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The review source is `BASE_SHA: 1111…`, `HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE` on every CR, including the re-review.

## 1. Initial CR

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Then record the review tree with the Fix-delta block. Use the whole block, keyed **wave1-CR**:

```bash
FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || { rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1; }
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
FD_STATUS=$?
rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
exit "$FD_STATUS"
```

The printed SHA is **T0**. If the block exits nonzero, stop dispatch and report the shell error.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<filled code-reviewer.md>
DESCRIPTION: Wave 1 / Task 1 - <implementer summary>
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Ask: production-ready?` })
```

The supplied report is `FIX_FIRST` with one Moderate and `Behaviour-change: yes`:

- This is review 1, so it has no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- The response is fix 1.
- No fan-out applies. There is a single finding, and an integrated wave before its commit gets one in-place worker.

## 2. Repair dispatch

This is a plain in-place worker. It carries the report verbatim and no commit or staging instruction.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "implementer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text + Tests: block + Files: paths>
Work from: /workspace/project
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
## Code review report to fix
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
<status protocol: DONE | DONE_WITH_CONCERNS | BLOCKED | NEEDS_CONTEXT>` })
```

Observed result: `DONE`, and the worker committed at `2222…`.

- That worker commit is irrelevant to review sourcing. `WAVE_BASE_SHA` stays `1111…`, `HEAD_SHA` stays `WORKTREE`, and the fold in step 5 absorbs the commit.
- The scoped rerun `(cd "/workspace/project" && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)` passes, as observed.

## 3. Repair-only delta, then SR first

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run the same Fix-delta block in `/workspace/project` and record **T1**. Then produce the delta:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T1>
```

This is tree-to-tree, never `1111..2222` and never a working-tree diff. It should contain only the `src/parse.mjs` fix and the new `tests/error.test.mjs`.

Because the report says `Behaviour-change: yes`, the reroute goes SR first:

- The SR is a first review: no `## Previous review report` marker, so no `TRAJECTORY:` line.
- Its ordinal continues the task's SR count. The initial SR was review 1, so this is **SR review 2**.
- It is post-integration, so it reviews the implementation worktree directly, with no snapshot.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "spec-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<full Task 1 text>
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10 (read the anchored range yourself)
Tests: <Task 1 Tests: block verbatim>  Test: tests/parse.test.mjs
Fix diff under review = the Fix delta below; start from its hunks, read touched files in full; never run tests.
## Fix delta
<output of git diff --binary T0 T1>` })
```

Supplied verdict: `COMPLIANT`. The CR step follows.

## 4. CR re-review (CR review 2; numbering unchanged)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A
```

Run the Fix-delta block again and record **T2**. It equals T1 because SR is read-only. Then produce the CR delta:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary <T0> <T2>
```

The delta runs from the prior CR's dispatch tree to this one.

```ts
subagent({ agent: "code-reviewer", async: false, cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `<filled code-reviewer.md>
DESCRIPTION: Wave 1 repair - empty string now rejected; tests/error.test.mjs added
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS: <full Task 1 text>
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes
<trajectory block from code-quality-reviewer-prompt.md, verbatim>
## Fix delta
<output of git diff --binary T0 T2>` })
```

Supplied verdict: `SHIP`. That is clean, so the loop ends. A `SHIP` report needs no `TRAJECTORY:` line and no further dispatch.

## 5. Fold and complete (only now)

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111" \
 && git -C /workspace/project add -A \
 && git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Task 1: parse numbers; reject empty string"
```

The soft reset folds the worker's `2222…` commit and all staged changes into one wave commit. That commit should contain `src/parse.mjs`, `tests/parse.test.mjs` and `tests/error.test.mjs`.

- If the commit would be empty, stop instead of completing.
- On success, call `plan_tracker` `update` to mark Task 1's existing index `complete`. The task stays `in_progress` until this point.
- The tree is left clean for the next wave.

## Empty repair delta

If `diff T0 T1` were empty, the fix changed no tracked file. A worker commit alone does not count; for example, `2222…` with an identical tree would still be empty. Ignored-only edits are also empty.

In that case:

1. Dispatch no SR or CR re-review.
2. Count a failed attempt under When a Subagent Fails.
3. Resend the prior report verbatim with "your fix changed no tracked file".
4. Stop after the two-attempt limit, with the task kept `in_progress`.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
The following are proposed commands and dispatches, not executed actions. `${TASK_1_FULL_TEXT}`, `${TESTS_BLOCK}`, and `${TEST_PATHS}` below mean the available verbatim task, Tests contract, and `- Test:` paths—not reconstructed requirements.

### 1. Initial integrated-wave code review

Keep the wave base fixed even if a worker later commits.

```bash
cd /workspace/project
WAVE_BASE_SHA=1111111111111111111111111111111111111111

# Each invocation runs the complete scratch-index capture block.
capture_review_tree() (
  FD_ROOT='/workspace/project'
  FD_INDEX=$(mktemp) || exit 1
  cp "$(git -C "$FD_ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path index)" "$FD_INDEX" || {
    rm -f "$FD_INDEX"; exit 1;
  }
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" add -A &&
    GIT_INDEX_FILE="$FD_INDEX" git -C "$FD_ROOT" write-tree
  FD_STATUS=$?
  rm -f "$FD_INDEX"
  exit "$FD_STATUS"
)

git add -A || exit 1
CR_BEFORE=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'wave-1 initial-CR tree: %s\n' "$CR_BEFORE"
```

Dispatch:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "code-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Use the supplied requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md template.
DESCRIPTION: Task 1 implementation; accepted initial spec review and passing
scoped tests. Integrated deliverables: src/parse.mjs, tests/parse.test.mjs.
PLAN_OR_REQUIREMENTS:
${TASK_1_FULL_TEXT}
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs
Review production readiness, including staged and unstaged changes against Base.
Do not edit files.`
})
```

The source is the integrated checkout against the fixed base, **not** a commit range. No wave commit yet.

### 2. Repair after the supplied `FIX_FIRST`

Use one in-place worker; no nested worktree or fan-out:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "implementer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Repair Task 1 in this checkout.
${TASK_1_FULL_TEXT}
Spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
TEST_CONTRACT:
${TESTS_BLOCK}
${TEST_PATHS}
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs

Verify the finding, reject empty input, and add the requested coverage.
Return explicitly DONE, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, NEEDS_CONTEXT, or BLOCKED,
with test-contract evidence and a self-review.

Prior review report, verbatim:
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes`
})
```

No commit or staging instruction is included in that repair payload.

Given the supplied `DONE`, worker commit `2222222222222222222222222222222222222222`, and passing scoped rerun, the gate command is:

```bash
(cd /workspace/project && node --test tests/parse.test.mjs)
```

After that successful gate:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
SR_AFTER=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'task-1 repair-SR tree: %s\n' "$SR_AFTER"
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary "$CR_BEFORE" "$SR_AFTER" \
  > /tmp/project-task1-repair-sr.diff
```

This tree-to-tree diff is the **repair-only delta**, including `src/parse.mjs` and new `tests/error.test.mjs`, regardless of the worker commit.

### 3. Behaviour-change reroute: SR first

Dispatch against the current integrated checkout:

```js
subagent({
  agent: "spec-reviewer",
  async: false,
  cwd: "/workspace/project",
  task: `
Review Task 1's behavior-changing repair as its next SR ordinal.
${TASK_1_FULL_TEXT}
Authoritative spec: /workspace/project/doc/specs/numbers.md:8-10
${TESTS_BLOCK}
${TEST_PATHS}
Additional touched test path: tests/error.test.mjs

## Fix delta
${contents_of_/tmp/project-task1-repair-sr.diff}

Start from diff hunks with file:line; read each touched file in full.
Assess the repair against the task and anchored spec. Never execute tests.`
})
```

This is a first review of the behavior-changing repair: **no previous-review marker and no trajectory requirement**. It carries the Tests contract, not scoped execution commands.

### 4. After supplied SR `COMPLIANT`, CR re-review

```bash
git -C /workspace/project add -A || exit 1
CR_AFTER=$(capture_review_tree) || exit 1
printf 'wave-1 CR re-review tree: %s\n' "$CR_AFTER"
git -C /workspace/project diff --binary "$CR_BEFORE" "$CR_AFTER" \
  > /tmp/project-wave1-repair-cr.diff
```

Dispatch `code-reviewer`, foreground, cwd `/workspace/project`, with the initial CR payload unchanged in review source:

```text
BASE_SHA: 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111
HEAD_SHA: WORKTREE
SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test tests/parse.test.mjs

## Previous review report (re-review trigger)
Verdict: FIX_FIRST
Moderate: src/parse.mjs accepts an empty string as zero; reject it and add coverage in tests/error.test.mjs.
Behaviour-change: yes

## Fix delta
[verbatim contents of /tmp/project-wave1-repair-cr.diff]
```

Append the supplied code-quality template’s complete **“Re-review: trajectory verdict”** block verbatim. Retain the full Task 1 requirements and description; note the repair SR was `COMPLIANT`.

### 5. Only after supplied CR `SHIP`

Fold the worker commit and all deliverables into one durable wave commit:

```bash
git -C /workspace/project reset --soft \
  1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 &&
git -C /workspace/project add -A &&
git -C /workspace/project commit -m "Implement number parsing and reject empty input"
```

Only after successful, nonempty commit:

```js
plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: 1, status: "complete" })
```

An **empty repair delta** means no tracked repair occurred relative to the initial review tree. Dispatch no re-review; count a failed attempt and resend the prior report with “your fix changed no tracked file,” subject to the two-attempt limit. A moved HEAD alone is not repair evidence.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved: After keeps BASE_SHA 1111…/HEAD_SHA WORKTREE on both CRs with add -A before each review, captures T0/T1/T2 through the seeded scratch-index write-tree block, diffs tree objects (explicitly rejecting 1111..2222 and working-tree diffs), dispatches one plain in-place implementer in /workspace/project with the verbatim report and no commit/staging instruction, routes the Behaviour-change repair through SR against /workspace/project with anchors, Tests contract and Fix delta before the CR re-review, runs only the scoped command, and folds via reset --soft / add -A / commit before the plan_tracker complete call, while treating an empty T0→T1 delta as a failed attempt with the task kept in_progress. Two small tightening points that would make After even more robust without affecting the Change: keep Before's explicit `plan_tracker({ action: "update", ... status: "complete" })` call rather than describing it in prose, and retain Before's SR instruction to read deleted files from the recorded base SHA, which makes the integrated-checkout (not per-patch snapshot) read source unambiguous.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and delivers the Change: both CR dispatches pin BASE_SHA to 1111… with HEAD_SHA WORKTREE after git add -A and review the integrated staged/unstaged checkout rather than a commit range; the seeded GIT_INDEX_FILE capture_review_tree helper records CR_BEFORE before the initial review and SR_AFTER/CR_AFTER after the gate, with git diff --binary between tree objects explicitly described as including src/parse.mjs and the new tests/error.test.mjs regardless of the worker's 2222… commit; the single in-place implementer in /workspace/project carries the verbatim FIX_FIRST report and no commit/staging/uncommitted instruction; the Behaviour-change: yes repair is routed through a plain affected-task SR against /workspace/project with the task, anchors, Tests contract and Fix delta before the CR re-review; the scoped command runs alone, the reset --soft/add -A/commit fold happens only after COMPLIANT and SHIP, and plan_tracker completion follows the nonempty commit; and the empty-delta paragraph treats a moved HEAD without tracked changes as a failed attempt. Nothing moved. Two small robustness notes for the wording: After relies on shell variables (CR_BEFORE, SR_AFTER, CR_AFTER) surviving across separate fenced blocks, whereas Before persisted tree SHAs to files under /tmp/project-wave1-review—adding a one-line note that captures are persisted (or writing them to files as Before did) would make the tree-capture record unambiguous to a reader executing the blocks independently; and the After re-review payload lists the previous report before the Fix delta, which is fine, but stating once that both the marker and the delta are appended to the otherwise unchanged initial CR payload (as Before does) would preempt any reading that the payload was reduced to only the three header lines shown.
